scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project.

sources.title: Lake County Economic Development Commission

sources.title: Development Agreement for Digital Crossroads of America Data Center and Technology Hub
sources.notes: Executed development agreement attached to the city resolution. Section 1.9(B) requires good-faith priority for Hammond, Lake County and Indiana contractors and workers, evidence about bids and awards, and quarterly compliance reporting to the Redevelopment Commission through construction completion. It also states prospective investment and job figures and water-permit capacities. The agreement does not itself report realized hiring, payroll, measured water use or confirmation that the permit transfer occurred.

sources.title: Principal Digital Real Estate Fund 2023 Annual Report — Audited Financial Statements
sources.notes: Audited fund statements describe the Hammond TIF bond and mirror loan, including the $8.04 million principal, 4% interest rate, 2044 maturity and 2022–2023 project TIF revenues applied to repayment. The arrangement is eliminated in the fund's consolidated statements.

sources.title: Principal Digital Real Estate Fund (A), LP 2025 Annual Report — Audited Financial Statements
sources.notes: Audited fund statements repeat the Hammond financing terms and report 2024-2025 project TIF revenues used toward loan repayments. The report states that these revenues were generated solely by real-estate tax payments made by Hammond Data Center. The audited consolidated schedule reports Hammond's 2024 and 2025 cost basis and fair value; the manager update reports 115,652 square feet, 15 MW commissioned and 89.3% leased and occupied at year-end 2025. The debt note reports asset-specific equipment line-of-credit balances. Its separate real-estate-improvements roll-forward covers the entire multi-property Aggregator and is not assigned to Hammond.

sources.title: Digital Crossroads finishes $40m Lake Michigan data center in Indiana
sources.notes: Contemporaneous trade-press completion report states that the operating facility employed 17 people and describes Lake Michigan water cooling. sources.title: Hammond Common Council Meeting Minutes — June 9, 2025
sources.notes: The official minutes record a statement by Decennial Group co-founder David Pavlik during Council consideration of the later 301 Digital Crossroads proposal. He describes the existing Building 1, acquired mid-construction in 2021, and reports well over $80 million spent with local contractors for electrical, mechanical, plumbing, roofing, re-roofing and fiber work. The amount is developer testimony preserved in a public record, not an audited expenditure schedule. The minutes do not define local geography, spending start date, payroll, worker count, job-years or multiplier effects.

sources.title: Hammond Ordinance 9496 — DX Hammond Economic Improvement District
sources.notes: The enacted ordinance and attached petition establish a 67.52-acre economic improvement district for privately funded project debt. Exhibit J-1 gives an $88,656,629 Building 1 capital-cost estimate. Section 46 caps annual special assessments at $3,415,000 in Zone 1 and $3,415,000 in Zone 2, with Zone 3 exempt; assessments may remain for up to 25 years after an EID bond is issued. The ordinance says City, state and political-subdivision faith, credit and taxing power are not pledged to EID debt, and excess zone expenses are payable by the project owner. No EID bond issuance, final assessment schedule, collections or expenditures were verified in this review. The attached U.S. Chamber typical-data-center multipliers are contextual and are not encoded as Hammond facts.

sources.title: IEDC Transparency Portal - DX Hammond Opco, LLC DATA agreement, project 419963
sources.notes: Current public portal record retrieved through the portal's JSON endpoint and reconciled to the linked 25-page Data Center Tax Exemption Agreement PDF. The portal reports project 419963 in Lake County, post-term reporting status, compliance, $28,369,398.27 paid/certified to date and $186,954,143 of actual qualified investment. The agreement's Exhibit A identifies 100 Digital Crossroads Drive in Hammond, a three-phase $200 million, 400,000-square-foot, 40 MW project, a $150 million minimum qualified investment and a December 31, 2024 investment deadline. project_updates.title: Proposed expansion agreement expired
project_updates.notes: Hammond reports that the development agreement for 301 Digital Crossroads expired after its June 30, 2026 deadline. The city says it will offer no further extensions of that agreement. The 2025 proposed expansion and associated payment promises are not treated as active commitments or realized receipts. This update concerns the proposed expansion; it does not establish closure of the existing DX-1 facility.

project_updates.title: Developer reports more than $80 million spent with local contractors
project_updates.notes: Official Council minutes record Decennial's co-founder describing more than $80 million spent with local contractors on the existing Building 1. The amount is a cumulative, developer-reported lower bound. Local geography, annual timing, contractor payments, worker counts, payroll and multiplier effects remain unverified.

project_updates.title: Owner-funded improvement district separates estimates from City credit
project_updates.notes: Ordinance 9496 estimates Building 1 capital expenditure at $88,656,629 and creates potential owner special assessments for project debt and district expenses. The ordinance does not pledge City or state faith, credit or taxing power, and assigns excess zone expenses to the project owner. The application retains the cost and assessment caps as forecasts because no final EID bond, schedule, collection or expenditure was verified.

project_updates.title: State debt register shows the existing TIF bond but no separate EID debt
project_updates.notes: Indiana Gateway's live Hammond Civil City outstanding-debt register includes the Series 2019 Data Center bond and no separately named DX Hammond Economic Improvement District or EID bond. This closes one public-record screen, not the entire financing question: a private obligation, unreported closing or separately administered instrument could fall outside the City register. EID bills, owner payments, district receipts and expenditures remain unverified.

project_updates.title: Unsubmitted 2025 annual report blocks the debt-series extension
project_updates.notes: Gateway's rendered output states that Hammond Civil City has not yet submitted its 2025 Annual Financial Report. No apparent 2025 export value is admitted as an economic record. The audited Series 2019 principal, interest, pledged-revenue, transfer and remaining-commitment histories therefore stop at 2024 pending a submitted annual report or equivalent audited statement.

project_updates.title: Audited report separates operating scale, private financing and fund accounting
project_updates.notes: Principal reports year-end cost basis, fair value, 115,652 square feet, 15 MW commissioned, 89.3% leased and occupied, and asset-specific equipment line-of-credit balances. Cost basis, fair value and private debt remain separate stocks; neither debt-balance changes nor the report's fund-wide real-estate-improvements roll-forward are treated as Hammond annual capital spending. Utilization is not converted into MW, revenue, employment or measured electricity use.

project_updates.title: Current operator factsheet broadens the documented benefit account

It also says it pays the full cost of campus energy and town water/wastewater service. These statements remain operator-reported: the profile does not convert them into audited annual spending, direct FTEs, verified rate impacts or metered resource use.

project_updates.title: State record links a water-line grant to existing and planned jobs
project_updates.notes: The Rural Infrastructure Authority approved a $148,900 grant to the Town of Forest City for an approximately 1,000-foot publicly owned water-line extension serving a new Facebook campus building. The same record reports 100 existing positions and ten planned jobs over two years. The grant, existing-position snapshot and forecast remain separate; approval does not establish final expenditure or realized hiring.

project_updates.title: Brownfield reuse adds community context
project_updates.notes: North Carolina DEQ identifies the data center as reuse of a former textile and boat-manufacturing site affected by contamination and vacancy, under a 2012 Brownfields Agreement. The agency's approximately 14% county-revenue statement is not encoded as a quantitative record because the current page gives no measurement date or denominator and the audited annual county series provides the more defensible fiscal evidence.

project_updates.title: Utility filing adds a qualified realized-investment descriptor
project_updates.notes: NIPSCO’s 2021 plan describes the operating Hammond facility as more than $50 million. The study records this as a qualified cumulative facility amount and leaves the 2018 initial-phase and full-build amounts in forecasts.

project_updates.title: City budget adds a separate personal-property assessment
project_updates.notes: Hammond’s adopted budget identifies DX Hammond JV LLC personal property at $30,328,680 for 2023 payable 2024, equal to 0.95% of city assessed value. It remains separate from the lease-area real-property series.

project_updates.title: Filed company testimony adds operating capacity and unquantified utility-design payments
project_updates.notes: DX Hammond states that the existing facility operates at 20 MW and that it had contracted with and paid NIPSCO several million dollars for feasibility, design and engineering for DX3. The capacity is not measured use. Because several million is not an exact or defensibly bounded value, no quantitative payment record is created; the related expansion agreement later expired.

project_updates.title: State permit adds backup-power equipment context
project_updates.notes: The permit lists eight diesel emergency generators, including three approved for construction in 2022. The application presents a permit equipment count rather than actual runtime, fuel use or emissions.

project_updates.title: County commission confirms 2019 revolving-loan support without a project amount
project_updates.notes: The current county page says the commission provided initial seed money in fall 2019. Because it gives no project-specific amount or terms, the support is retained as qualitative history and contributes no economic record.

project_updates.title: Audited fund statements confirm the TIF financing and repayment structure
project_updates.notes: The fund's audited statements confirm an $8.04 million City loan, its mirrored TIF bond and annual project TIF revenues applied to repayment. These amounts are presented as public-financing flows rather than a grant or general-fund revenue, and the annual repayments are not combined with gross parcel distributions.

project_updates.title: Development agreement adds a job forecast, local-labor requirements and water-permit limits
project_updates.notes: The agreement anticipated approximately 40 full-time jobs and required good-faith priority for Hammond, Lake County and Indiana contractors and workers. Section 1.9(B)(2) also required the developer to retain relevant compliance data and provide it to the Redevelopment Commission at least quarterly until construction completion. The study treats the jobs as a forecast, the labor terms as requirements without realized participation data, and the water figures as permit capacities rather than use.

project_updates.title: Contemporaneous completion report supplies a 17-employee operating snapshot
project_updates.notes: Data Center Dynamics reported 17 facility employees and separately described an expectation that customer staff could bring on-site employment to roughly 40. Only the 17-person snapshot is recorded as reported activity; the article's cooling description has no measured water volume.

project_updates.title: City audit establishes the data-center bond's pre-amortization baseline
project_updates.notes: At year-end 2022 the City reported $8.04 million of outstanding Series 2019 principal, no principal retired, $321,600 of interest and fees and $12,074,400 of future principal-plus-interest commitment. Pledged TIF revenue, the debt-service-fund transfer and the private fund's loan-repayment amount retain their separate labels.

project_updates.title: Audited principal amortization begins in 2023
project_updates.notes: The Series 2019 Data Center fund retired $65,000 of principal and reported $321,600 of interest and fees in 2023, leaving $7.975 million outstanding. The audit's $522,816 pledged-revenue figure and $349,574 fund transfer are not recast as the private fund's $225,800 project-tax repayment amount.

project_updates.title: City audit traces 2024 debt service and the original bond draws
project_updates.notes: The City reports $165,000 of principal retired, $317,700 of interest and fees and $7.81 million of year-end principal in 2024. It also documents $5 million issued in 2019 and the remaining $3.04 million drawn in 2020. These financing flows are not treated as additional project investment or grants.

project_updates.title: Design-build contractor documents the completed first-facility scope
project_updates.notes: ARCO identifies its completed 105,000-square-foot data-center and central-utility-plant project, including site development, utility installation and major equipment procurement. This establishes a contractor role and work scope without supplying contract payments, payroll, job-years, worker residence or a new investment amount.

project_updates.title: Indiana electrical contractor identifies the first-phase installation scope
project_updates.notes: EMCOR Hyre reports electrical-design coordination and installation of the substation, generators, transformers, switchboards, transfer switches, UPS systems, conduit, cable and controls. Its less-than-five-month first-phase timing is not converted into job-years, and the page gives no payment or payroll amount.

project_updates.title: A 2024 data-hall buildout adds dated construction-supply-chain evidence
project_updates.notes: Executive Construction reports completing final commissioning and integrated systems testing for a later Digital Crossroad data-hall buildout and names EMCOR Hyre Electric and AMS Industries as trade partners. The update supports continuing construction activity and a supplier roster, but no expenditure, workforce, payroll or worker-residence total.

project_updates.title: Engineering case study adds design and cooling-system supplier roles
project_updates.notes: AHA identifies consulting, master-planning, MEP/fire-protection design, visualization and renewable-energy services for the Hammond campus. Its water-and-air cooling description is design evidence, not metered withdrawal, consumption or contractor economic totals.

project_updates.title: State contract table separates the incentive cap, payment status and job expectations
project_updates.notes: IEDC project 419942 reports a $750,000 EDGE contract, 45 expected new jobs by contract end and $0 paid or certified to date at the 2018 cutoff. The commitment and job expectation remain forecasts; the zero is a dated cumulative program-status observation and does not establish later claims or realized employment.

project_updates.title: State award sheet adds one bounded public charging-infrastructure commitment
project_updates.notes: IDEM lists Digital Crossroads for one Level 2 charging location and an $8,000 award. The application records the award as public-cost evidence while leaving payment, installation, ownership and use unverified.

project_updates.title: Annual state reports bound when Hammond's incentive balances changed
project_updates.notes: IEDC's 2018 and 2021-2025 compliance reports turn the current incentive totals into dated cumulative snapshots. EDGE rose from $0 in 2018 to $11,763 by 2021 and stayed there through contract end; IRTC was fully certified by 2021; DATA reported $0 paid/certified in 2023, a blank paid/certified field but $0 actual qualified investment in 2024, then $28,369,398.27 paid/certified with $186,954,143 of actual qualified investment in 2025. Repeated balances are not annual flows, and the reports do not disclose transaction dates or establish realized EDGE employment.

project_updates.title: State portal verifies qualified investment and separates the sales-tax exemption
project_updates.notes: IEDC project 419963 reports $186,954,143 of actual qualified investment and $28,369,398.27 paid/certified to date under the DATA agreement. The agreement set a $150 million minimum for the original three-phase $200 million campus plan. Investment, exemption value, assessed value and local contractor spending remain separate measures.

project_updates.title: Industrial-recovery credit reaches the portal's full certified amount
project_updates.notes: IEDC project 419963 reports the $9,045,773.82 Industrial Recovery Tax Credit maximum as paid/certified to date, with compliant post-term status. The account treats the contractual cap as a forecast and the cumulative certification as an observed public-cost status; neither is local revenue or cash construction spending.

project_updates.title: Current EDGE record closes with a small certified amount and no realized-job proof
project_updates.notes: IEDC reports that project 419942 ended September 27, 2023 with $11,763 paid/certified, a displayed negative $5,209 adjustment and compliant status. The portal repeats 45 expected jobs by 2025 and lists $239,530,500 of expected qualified investment, but those remain forecasts. Its zero actual-investment field is not treated as zero campus investment because the program scope differs and the DATA record separately verifies qualified investment.

project_updates.title: County industry series adds a noncausal employment and payroll benchmark
project_updates.notes: County Business Patterns supplies eight reference years of Lake County establishments, March employment and annual payroll for NAICS 518210. The series covers the entire county industry, includes hosting and data-processing businesses beyond data centers, and carries moderate or high noise flags in several cells. It is presented as community context around the Hammond opening, not as Digital Crossroad employment, payroll, job creation or a causal effect.

project_updates.title: Quarterly local-labor records have a defined acquisition path
project_updates.notes: The 2018 agreement required quarterly reporting to the Redevelopment Commission on compliance with its Hammond, Lake County and Indiana contractor and worker priorities. No named filing was located in the City’s indexed public document archive, whose Redevelopment Commission categories begin in 2021. This is an unresolved records-acquisition target, not evidence of noncompliance or zero local participation. A request should seek the existing quarterly submissions, bidder and award records, and any Commission review correspondence without asking the City to create a new analysis.

project_updates.title: Five-year audit adds jobs, wages and capital expenditure for the Storey agreement
project_updates.notes: Nevada GOED identifies Switch, LTD #2 as a new Storey County data-center project and marks its December 31, 2020 five-year audit compliant. The state reports 111 jobs, a $50.97 average hourly wage and $179,943,184 of capital expenditure. The Clark County #3 row repeats the same findings, so the application preserves the official Storey allocation while flagging the duplication and withholding any Tahoe Reno 1 building allocation.

project_updates.title: Core Citadel parcel adds real-estate values and completed tax payments
project_updates.notes: Storey County parcel 005-012-23 identifies 1 Superloop Circle and three data-center modules totaling 575,985 listed square feet. The release adds separate 2024–2026 real-property value stocks, three parcel tax bills, two completed fiscal-year payments and the first paid installment of the open 2026–2027 year. Tenant-equipment accounts and CM001611 remain separate to prevent double counting.

project_updates.title: County minutes report a separate $356,000 Switch donation
project_updates.notes: The Fire District reported a $356,000 donation from Switch in April 2025. The minutes do not identify its purpose and discuss the ladder-truck purchase separately, so the application preserves it as an unassigned company-county contribution.

project_updates.title: Fire Chief reports more than $2 million from Switch for Station 75 ladder truck
project_updates.notes: The September 2025 minutes report a Switch contribution greater than $2 million for the ladder truck. The amount remains a lower bound, and the expected twelve-month delivery means the record does not claim the truck was already in service.

project_updates.title: Fire capital plan exposes a public cost paired with the donated truck
project_updates.notes: The Fire District plans $100,000 in fiscal 2026–2027 to equip Pierce Truck 75 and identifies the truck as purchased by Switch. The application records the district amount as a forecast public cost, preserving both sides of the transaction without netting unlike periods.

project_updates.title: Nine-year electricity series documents operating growth without converting use into cost
project_updates.notes: Apple reports Mesa electricity use rising from 45 million kWh in fiscal 2017 to 563 million kWh in fiscal 2025. The same report says Apple took operational control in October 2015, the converted data center began servicing customers in March 2017, and supporting renewable resources include the 50 MW Bonnybrooke solar project and 4.67 MW of onsite PV. Use is operator-reported rather than utility-meter verified; generation capacity is not load, annual output, avoided cost or capital spending.

project_updates.title: Finaled permits document conversion, expansion and water-system work
project_updates.notes: Mesa permit rows identify Apple-era data halls, the Tilden AZ4 expansion, instrument-air, domestic-water, chilled/condenser-water, emergency makeup-water and soft-water-treatment scopes at parcel 30433005S. The application retains eight finaled or certificate-issued permit valuations individually. It excludes related addenda, Issued-only records and pre-Apple industrial work; no permit values are summed or treated as verified expenditures.

project_updates.title: Current FTZ agreement links the premises to data-center and equipment activities
project_updates.notes: The Council-approved operator agreement identifies Apple Inc. and 3740 S Signal Butte Road and permits local data-center operations plus data-center-equipment assembly and high-tech manufacturing or storage of FTZ goods. It specifies a $1,000 activation fee and $5,000 annual administration fee, but the reviewed form has blank execution dates and no evidence of payment. No FTZ savings amount is inferred, and the agreement does not merge the separate real-property and business-personal-property accounts.

project_updates.title: Water-treatment implementation is documented without a Mesa savings claim
project_updates.notes: Apple describes resin-treatment and sphagnum-moss work being implemented at Mesa, but its percentage reductions come from a pilot elsewhere and are not Mesa facility measurements. The study therefore adds no quantitative Mesa water-use or water-savings record. Permit descriptions establish system work, not consumption or avoided use.
